chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Furat, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in one of his speeches: 'Beware of ingratitude to the parents, for the aroma of Paradise is found from a travel distance of a thousand years, and it will not be found by the ungrateful one, nor by a severer of kinship ties, nor by an elderly adulterer, nor by one who drags his garment in pride. Indeed, greatness belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'

key_terms.جَارُّ إِزَارِهِ: One who drags his garment (symbol of pride)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for being grateful to parents according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith links the spiritual reward of filial piety to the tangible sensory experience of Paradise, emphasizing that ingratitude (uquq) acts as a barrier to its scent. It expands the scope of exclusion to include those who sever kinship ties (qat' al-rahim) and the arrogant, clarifying that while humans may possess pride, ultimate 'greatness' (al-kibriya) is an exclusive attribute of Allah, a concept central to Shia theological understanding of divine majesty.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Furat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said in a speech of his<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Beware of ingratitude to the parents, for the aroma of the Paradise would be found from a travel distance of a thousand years, and it will not be found by the ungrateful one, nor by a severer of the relationships, nor a elderly adulterer, nor by a dragger of his trousers (pompous one). But rather, the Greatness is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the worlds’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Furat from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said in one of his speeches, ‘Beware of causing suffering and disappointment to parents. The fragrance of paradise can be sensed from a distance of a one thousand year journey, but those causing suffering and disappointments to parents, those failing to maintain good relations with relatives, an old fornicating man and one who drags his garments out of arrogance and boastfulness will not sense such fragrance. Greatness belongs only to Allah, Lord of the worlds.’”
